accepted.deprecationClaim: User scope direction; game Intel deprecation has not been verified
accepted.priority: make UI development and iteration easier

proposed.engineHost: in-process CLI/Tauri with deferred normal exit and durable forced-termination recovery

sharedFileOwners.requiredWorkerBehavior: Submit integration requests for shared files instead of opportunistic edits.

architecture: bridge-contracts: versioned DTOs/events/errors and generated frontend types
bridge-domain: pure decisions and capability projections
bridge-engine: operation owner and ports, no Tauri
bridge-cli/AXF and Tauri: thin clients of same dispatcher
ui: replaceable frontend with real/mock client adapters
executionRules: Contract changes have one integrator; consumers use frozen fixtures/types.
Workers lease narrow declared write scopes. Cargo/pnpm locks, composition, CI, provider contracts and shared session/game paths have one owner at a time.
Root serializes shared workspace files and final integration. Dependency-ready does not mean safe to edit concurrently.
Each work package becomes an issue and repo-scoped packet with exact source inputs before implementation. No invented branches/worktrees.
Review PRs using the owning repo review gate; review correction deltas and required checks on exact head.
An acceptance dispatcher runs every declared suite for its work package and aggregates per-host receipts; a single-suite pass cannot mark a multi-suite package accepted.
Qualify gates on matching native hosts. Aggregate independently retained receipts; never execute a Mac gate on Windows and label it Mac.
Re-resolve host cwd and regenerate execution-bound plans for that owner; scheduling plan is not a cross-repo bulk execution command.
Runner prepare/start remain disabled in this session. Use normal explicitly enabled governed execution later, never bypass mutation policy.

blockers.detail: No macOS executor attached to this session. Bind an actual Apple Silicon host, native CI jobs and owning canonical checkouts before Mac execution. Record actual game/runtime/companion architectures on that host.
Registration/setup/launch/update platform unavailable/unqualified in current Profiles source; br-08/10/11 close these.
Current upstream loader chooses launcher INI and forwards executable-only argv; br-09 required.
Package/channel/publisher/mac signing/notary and architecture/runtime pairing decisions owned by br-00/23.
Qualification scripts/Cargo/frontend suites are future task deliverables. Validation/order success is not implementation acceptance.
No new issues/branches/PRs created by planning. Bind each package to its owning repo issue before implementation; branch change/worktree creation requires user authorization.

milestones.title: Usable mock frontend before native game integration
Packaged integration with parity and recovery
Both operating systems qualified and cut over

packages.title: Product scope, ownership and operating contract
deliverables: Supersede Windows/WPF ownership for the new Bridge; do not relocate existing mac launcher or mod runtime.
Ratify first-release journeys, architecture matrix, frontend default and native dependency responsibilities.
Record proposed in-process engine hosting and safe normal-exit versus forced-termination recovery rules.
Map existing behavior/test scenarios into requirements without preserving C# implementation.
Create the fail-closed qualification dispatcher and gate inventory; record unavailable host/script/receipt as blocked, never success.
acceptanceCriteria: Required host matrix is Windows x64 and Apple Silicon macOS; shell/game/native module architectures are matched explicitly. Intel Mac host qualification is excluded by user direction.
Shared Profiles remains sole owner of catalog/storage/exclusion/game update; runtime producers retain their source/artifact ownership.
Shuttle Bay and Engineering share selected target and draft semantics; ordinary and isolated requests remain distinct.
Scope includes launch/catalog, game and mod management, settings/Data Sync, support and Bridge update; dormant Battle activation is an optional later extension.
Review records distinguish accepted decisions, proposed frontend details and implementation evidence.

packages.title: Rust/frontend workspace and native CI foundations
deliverables: Cargo workspace, locked dependencies, Rust toolchain pin, frontend package lock and native Tauri shell.
Define Windows x64 and Apple Silicon native CI jobs and receipt collection; record unresolved host bindings without claiming a native job ran.
Implement cargo fmt/clippy/test and frontend typecheck/test/build gate definitions; qualified gate dispatcher refuses wrong-host/missing output.
acceptanceCriteria: Fresh clean local host can run supported foundation development commands using exact pins.
Core/engine dependency graph contains no Tauri/webview/DOM packages.
Select and pin native UI automation: current Tauri documentation supports embedded WebdriverIO on macOS; plain tauri-driver alone cannot provide that Mac coverage.
UI mock startup requires neither game nor native library nor Rust compilation.
Native host bindings are recorded as resolved or unresolved; unresolved Mac execution blocks native gates, while workspace and mock development can continue.

packages.title: Versioned domain protocol and scenario fixtures
deliverables: Typed commands/queries/events/errors, explicit install/profile/session targets, preparation tokens and revision expectations.
Generated TypeScript types, JSON golden fixtures and complete required scenario catalog.
Ports for Profiles, native platform services, artifacts, configuration and lifetime custody.
acceptanceCriteria: Contradictory targets, unsupported version and malformed/unknown commands fail explicitly.
Requests and events carry request/operation IDs; snapshots carry revision and events monotonic sequence.
Commit idempotency keys bind exact input; replay after response loss returns original operation/status, while conflicting reuse rejects.
Prepare tokens bind target/revisions/artifact/schema identity and expire across restart; they do not grant permission or locks.
Backend facts/action availability contain no colors, controls, UI copy or window handles.
Scenarios cover ready/missing/offline/busy/unknown/multiple sessions/stale/failed/no-change/recovery.

packages.title: Typed frontend client and deterministic mock transport
deliverables: Renderer-neutral backend client with generated types and mock/real transport seam.
Browser development mode with fixture picker, simulated progress/latency/faults and reconnection.
acceptanceCriteria: UI runs from frontend tooling alone with no game, native binary, account data or backend.
Mock responses validate against exact protocol schema and share fixtures with engine tests.
Mocks preserve captured targets, errors/revisions/event ordering rather than replacing policy with happy-path stubs.
Production build excludes test bypasses and mock mutation hosts.

packages.title: Operation ownership, journal and recovery kernel
deliverables: Headless Rust command dispatcher, prepared-plan registry, resource admission, durable operation/journal state and event stream.
Deterministic fake ports for contention, cancellation, crash/restart and idempotent recovery.

Choose and record process custody: first release hosts the engine within each CLI/Tauri process; safe shutdown retains admitted work until completion, while abrupt process death requires durable recovery. A daemon is a separate later design decision.
acceptanceCriteria: Losing writer returns busy before downloads/staging/backups/journals; one exact mutation owner.
Commit revalidates physical/revision identities while retaining owning exclusions.
Webview/CLI disconnect cannot release the writing worker lease; cancellation is requested/cancelled-before-commit/too-late/committed/recovery-required.
Normal host close during native work defers process exit until safe durable state; forced process kill leaves restart recovery, never a claim that work continued after death.
Commit replay after response loss resolves original operation without a second mutation; conflicting input with the same idempotency key rejects.
Uncommitted plans invalidate on restart; admitted durable work remains inspectable by operation ID.
Fault injection at every durable boundary yields committed, rolled-back or explicit recovery-required state.

packages.title: Safe Profiles/TOML native consumers
deliverables: Versioned Rust FFI consumers of canonical native JSON and shared TOML operations.
Immutable source/native pins, per-target module hash receipts, buffer/lease ownership and module lifetime.
acceptanceCriteria: No second catalog, account store, game patch engine or native writer authority.
Return buffers/handles released through originating module; module stays loaded until last native lease/response ends.
Bounded malformed-response/version/non-ASCII/native-error tests and real ABI tests independently on each target.
Synchronous native update work can outlive await/client; cancellation never pretends the worker stopped.

packages.title: Windows platform services
deliverables: Native identity/process/filesystem/protected-state/signature/focus/shortcut adapters behind shared ports.
acceptanceCriteria: Exact file/directory and PID/start/executable identity; unknown observations remain unknown.
Alias/replacement/same-bytes-different-file and process reuse/exited-process tests pass on Windows.
Retained resource and flush/replace/recovery semantics match documented native guarantees.
Ordinary user scope; mod, official game and Bridge update trust domains remain separate.

packages.title: macOS platform services
deliverables: Native bundle/process/filesystem/Keychain/signature/focus/menu/shortcut adapters behind the same ports.
acceptanceCriteria: Canonical bundle/executable/physical identity and alias/case rules use actual macOS semantics.
Native Apple Silicon host cases verify process identity, replacement, permissions and durability; actual game/runtime architectures are recorded.
No Windows path/version/signature assumption or automatic Rosetta parity.
Unavailable platform feature is explicit; renderer does not decide operational policy by OS name.

packages.title: Profiles macOS identity, ordinary setup and protected-state foundation
deliverables: Canonical Mac ordinary setup kind and owner identity, installation registration/custody and lifetime exclusions.
Keychain/consent/persistence and browser/companion lifecycle implementation and synthetic native tests.
Publish exact dependency source/native receipts for producer and Bridge consumers; bindings follow shared contract.
acceptanceCriteria: Replace platform_unavailable for accepted Mac registration/ordinary setup with native qualified behavior.
No display-name inference or relabeling windows-user as a Mac profile kind.
Rename/replacement/symlink/concurrent-client admission cases run on actual native Macs.
Synthetic Keychain tests use ephemeral test Keychains; no developer login Keychain setup or real preference fixtures.
Browser child/callback identity, abnormal exit and archive exclusion are tested; same-profile duplicate refused.

packages.title: Producer macOS explicit loader and artifact contract
deliverables: Owning mod loader accepts explicit installation/profile/store/config/log request and forwards exact argv.
Per-architecture runtime/loader manifests, identity and loading/signature/entitlement contract.
Integrate an exact Profiles dependency in the owning producer bootstrap/config/hooks/build; consume reusable hooks without moving their authority into Bridge.
acceptanceCriteria: No implicit official-launcher INI selection when host supplies exact target.
Environment/DYLD handling and loading restrictions are specified and tested on actual target architecture.
Requested isolation either activates with attributed readiness or fails; spawn never claims login.
No source move into Bridge; other providers need their own compatible artifact evidence.

packages.title: Profiles macOS coordinated launch and lifetime qualification
deliverables: Ordinary and isolated launch, attributed session readiness, store-mode failure, companion placement and lifetime writer custody.
acceptanceCriteria: Replace launch_unqualified only after actual native-host loading and session receipts.
Two distinct isolated IDs from one executable; same-ID duplicate refusal; reverse restart persistence.
Sign-in callbacks, CLI companion architecture, abnormal child exit, stopped archive/restore and client-close ownership are qualified.
Session identity uses exact executable/start/PID; account login remains a separate observed outcome.

packages.title: Profiles macOS game updater route and recovery
deliverables: Research exact official Mac metadata/image/version/signature route; implement direct updater or a qualified managed official-updater handoff.
Shared status/check/admission/update/recovery contract with Mac journal rules.
acceptanceCriteria: Direct-update feasibility decision is recorded with payload evidence; a handoff must honestly report what it can observe/control.
Replace unsupported_platform for required first-release journeys only with qualified behavior.
Stopped-install exclusion, archive/extraction containment, interruption, rollback and journal admission pass on native hosts.
Checked target version and install are immutable through the operation; Windows version/image rules are not reused.
No direct-update claim if first-release implementation uses managed handoff.

packages.title: Design system and accessible frontend primitives
deliverables: Svelte/TypeScript/Vite proposed default, reusable tokens/themes/navigation/dialogs/status/progress/form components.
Browser component gallery and reviewed visual/focus scenarios for both OS conventions.
Implement and freeze shared selected-target, draft, operation and navigation context interfaces before parallel screen work.
acceptanceCriteria: System/light/dark, keyboard, focus restoration, reduced motion, high contrast, 200% text and long labels.
Layout/copy/style edits hot reload without rebuilding Rust or requiring native integration.
Native window conventions expressed at thin shell boundary; UI components contain no filesystem/process policy.
Component/visual/automated accessibility suites plus recorded UX review; screenshots alone cannot approve behavior.

packages.title: Domain capability and observation projections
deliverables: Pure read models for targets/providers/features/operational availability with stable reason codes and diagnostics provenance.
acceptanceCriteria: Facts, policy and supported capability stay distinct; missing/invalid manifests do not grant support.
Provider IDs select behavior; display names never branch operational policy.
Preference is next-launch intent and cannot rewrite running session or captured operation.
Read-only projections do not bootstrap stores, mutate preferences, launch game or sidecars.

packages.title: Configuration/Data Sync draft and transaction engine
deliverables: Schema-driven semantic sparse TOML drafts, preview/validate/Save/Discard/restore/history and migration participants.
Settings and Data Sync share the same exact target/document draft.
acceptanceCriteria: Unknown keys/comments survive; inherited/default removal is first-class.
Missing config creates nothing until meaningful Save; no-change produces explicit outcome.
External modification/replacement/stale revision retains draft and rejects commit; same bytes do not erase physical target identity.
Save advances baseline once; failures/cancel/discard do not silently drop edits.
Backup/restore and profile lifecycle use canonical native lease/resource boundaries.

packages.title: Provider/runtime install, source switch and recovery
deliverables: Fresh per-OS runtime deploy/install/update/repair/adopt/remove transaction and ownership journal.
Source switch coordinates configuration participants through defined prepare/commit/compensation seam.
acceptanceCriteria: Reviewed digest/size/version/source/platform/signer evidence binds exact artifact before mutation.
External/replaced/unowned runtime cannot be removed as managed; adopted bytes restored on rollback.
Fault injection at each durable boundary, stale plans, same-byte replacement and source/config switch compensation.
Provider support is independently qualified by OS/architecture; one bootstrap/profile product per installation.

packages.title: Windows session and game-client application slice
deliverables: Explicit ordinary/isolated launch/focus/session observation and canonical game status/check/update/recover adapter.
acceptanceCriteria: Selection changes cannot retarget an admitted launch/update; recycled PID cannot be focused/cycled.
Spawn/isolation readiness/login are separate; unavailable observations block dependent mutation.
Every session using target is excluded from update; checked install/version survives selection change.
Synchronous native mutation continues to final outcome despite client disconnect.

packages.title: macOS session and game-client application slice
deliverables: Implement same application commands with qualified Mac catalog/loader/update capabilities.
acceptanceCriteria: Real Mac ordinary/isolated launch and exact process/readiness semantics match protocol.
Mac game route is truthful direct-update or managed handoff; outcome never overstates completion.
Mac lifetime/exclusion/recovery tests use real native modules and installed candidate topology.
First-release capability matrix reconciled for Apple Silicon hosts and their explicitly qualified game/runtime architectures.

packages.title: Shuttle Bay/Home and shared navigation against mocks
deliverables: Outcome-first Home, one visible target/profile selection and ordinary/isolated session views.
Separate game, mod and Bridge maintenance journeys with consistent action feedback.
acceptanceCriteria: Ready/missing/offline/running/unknown/multiple processes/recovery cases are usable without backend.
View switching preserves drafts; target changes use Save/Discard/Stay.
Primary action and warnings use typed backend facts and reasons, not duplicated operational policy.
Private paths absent in ordinary UI; diagnostics are explicit.

packages.title: Engineering/settings workspace against mocks
deliverables: Reusable schema controls, categories/search, sparse overrides/defaults, validation/restart notices, Data Sync editing.
acceptanceCriteria: All semantic field types and error/no-change/loading/stale/failed-save fixtures covered.
External changes preserve drafts; target transitions and Save/Discard behavior remain visible and accessible.
Screen development does not wait for br-14 engine implementation.
Backend schema remains authoritative; no handwritten duplicate TOML feature list.

packages.title: Management, confirmation, recovery and support UI against mocks
deliverables: Profile/install/provider management, prepared-plan confirmation, progress/recovery/history/diagnostic export and Bridge update views.
acceptanceCriteria: Plan shows captured target/scope; changing selection cannot change confirmed work.
Duplicate submission, requested/too-late cancellation, no-change/failure/recovery all have coherent feedback.
Diagnostic preview/redaction/opt-in paths and token filtering fixtures pass.
No native game/account material is needed for component and journey tests.

packages.title: Headless CLI/AXF and real Tauri protocol adapter
deliverables: CLI structured commands and thin Tauri command/event adapter sharing the same Rust dispatcher.
Frontend reconnect/resnapshot, event subscription and deterministic test host.
acceptanceCriteria: CLI resolves target, reviews/prepares/commits fixture change, streams events and restarts/recovers without linking Tauri.
Pure mock/CLI conformance runs on ordinary CI; actual Tauri invoke/event/reconnect conformance runs independently on Windows x64 and Apple Silicon using native shell receipts.
Production artifact excludes test host/mock bypass; Tauri capability allowlist limited to required adapter.
Closing UI follows engine safe shutdown; actual transaction custody remains with worker.
Reconnect after lost commit response reuses original operation; normal close during native mutation and forced-host-kill/restart both reach honest outcomes.

packages.title: Diagnostics, history and application support engine
deliverables: Redacted diagnostic preview/export, application preferences/history and service ownership interfaces.
Keep dormant Battle/sidecar activation outside initial release unless br-00 explicitly adds qualified scope.
acceptanceCriteria: Preview bytes match exported bytes; secrets/account contents/default private paths excluded.
Read-only support queries do not launch sinks/sidecars or mutate configs.
Per-user app preferences do not become mod TOML; recovery retains exact operation ownership.
Known/unavailable capability and cleanup failures remain visible.

packages.title: Platform package identity, native pairing and build pipeline
deliverables: Per-target Bridge packages, paired native dependencies/companions and immutable source/build receipts.
Windows installer/update identity and Mac app/DMG identity, signing/notarization pipeline and release-asset inspection.
Document transition from existing MSIX identity; no automatic change to trust/publisher roots.
acceptanceCriteria: Each Windows x64 / Apple Silicon Mac arm64 package includes matching architecture/pins and rejects missing/mismatched native bytes; game/runtime/companions match the actual selected process architecture.
Exact final signed/notarized bytes hashed; no universal or Intel-host package is required.
Three trust domains kept independent; installer signing/updater signatures do not establish provider/game artifact authority.
Clean-host install/storage/permission/uninstall behavior and retained external data verified.
Publisher/signing/notary/channel decisions and credential provisioning are recorded prerequisites, not invented approvals.

packages.title: Independent Bridge self-update and recovery engine
deliverables: Fresh Bridge release selection/verification/staging/replacement and recovery on both platforms.
acceptanceCriteria: Mod/provider authority cannot authorize Bridge update; helpers/native payloads remain exact paired identities.
Candidate/plan reverified before replacement; updater cannot mutate game/catalog roots.
Interrupted update, denied access, stale package and downgrade/withdrawal policy produce explicit outcomes.
New installer/channel migration is qualified per OS, not inferred from Tauri updater support.

packages.title: Mock UX milestone and independent design review
deliverables: Review complete first-release mock journeys with failure/progress/draft fixtures and both OS layouts.
Record usability/accessibility findings and correction deltas before native binding dominates the work.
acceptanceCriteria: Reviewers can run all normal/error/recovery flows without Rust/game/native prerequisites.
Player can identify exact intended target, next action, unsaved edits and recovery choice.
No unresolved blocking UX/keyboard/privacy issue; baselines bound to exact frontend commit.
Automated schema/screenshots alone do not stand in for reviewed UX.

packages.title: Integrated user journeys and multi-client contention
deliverables: Bind real engine results to UI with identical protocol fixtures; whole-journey tests across CLI/Tauri/native adapters.
Install/profile/config/mod/game/Bridge update and recovery fixture flows, captured target/revision/receipt checks.
acceptanceCriteria: UI and CLI agree on normalized outcomes; UI/CLI race yields one writer and no losing-client durable side effect.
Read/prepare/confirm/commit/reconnect/restart/recover preserve operation target and draft boundaries.
All new engine gates implemented and tested; no placeholder successful commands.
Windows x64 and Apple Silicon Mac integrations independently pass before platform release UX.

packages.title: Windows packaged UI and live journey qualification
deliverables: Actual signed packaged WebView2 client tests, Narrator/keyboard/high contrast/DPI and first-run/update/recovery.
Explicit live game/profile lifecycle qualification using approved test identities and exact target/artifact/client receipts.
acceptanceCriteria: Qualify exact Windows x64 signed bytes/OS/client/WebView runtime, not browser mock or old WPF result.
Ordinary launch, two isolated IDs, duplicate refusal, restart persistence, callbacks, archive/restore and shared-install update exclusion.
Safe fixture accounts/state used; real credentials/preferences never copied to test artifacts.
Blocking accessibility/runtime/identity/recovery issues corrected and independently re-reviewed.

packages.title: Apple Silicon packaged UI and live journey qualification
deliverables: Actual signed/notarized WKWebView client on native Apple Silicon and independent live journey/accessibility evidence.
acceptanceCriteria: App/game/mod/companions architecture matrix is explicit; native arm64 shell alone does not qualify x86 game/runtime under translation.
Same required lifecycle/update/recovery/callback/consent journeys, exact signed bytes and host/client/runtime receipts.
VoiceOver/native keyboard/window/scaling acceptance recorded; native automation route is qualified and accessibility also has manual evidence.
Test-only embedded WebDriver/IPC mocking plugins, if selected, are absent from final shipped artifacts; production signed packages receive independent smoke/UX qualification.
Translation-based route, if required by game architecture, separately qualified and labeled.

packages.title: Release readiness, independent review and old-stack retirement
deliverables: Independent implementation/security/UX review and correction reviews on exact final heads and artifact hashes.
Cross-platform release docs/support/recovery/installer migration, signed immutable dependency/source records.
Retire superseded WPF product/build paths as part of reviewed cutover; no requirement to preserve its implementation.
acceptanceCriteria: Both required host evidence lanes complete with no unresolved blocker; partial native capability cannot count as cross-platform release.
No unknown or failed required gate is bypassed; stale source/artifact evidence forces only affected checks to repeat.
Release/signing/publication follow owning repo/user authority; planning graph grants no eligibility or authority.
Old instructions/UX update delegation explicitly reconciled with new product contract.
